Update the Starlight Tailwind integration to use the updated sans-serif font stack from Tailwind CSS 3.4.x. Ensure the generated CSS reflects this change consistently, regardless of Tailwind's CSS reset setting, while keeping other CSS variables unchanged.

*   Modify the Starlight Tailwind integration:
    *   Set the `--sl-font` CSS custom property to `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif, "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji", "Segoe UI Symbol", "Noto Color Emoji"`.
    *   Remove the old font stack values including `-apple-system`, `BlinkMacSystemFont`, `"Segoe UI"`, `Roboto`, `"Helvetica Neue"`, `Arial`, `"Noto Sans"`, and `sans-serif` after `system-ui`.
    *   Ensure the updated `--sl-font` value is used both with and without Tailwind's preflight reset styles.
*   Maintain all other CSS custom properties:
    *   Ensure `--sl-font-mono` and all `--sl-color-*` variables remain unchanged.
*   Update the Tailwind CSS peer dependency:
    *   Set the version to `^3.4.1` or higher in the `@astrojs/starlight-tailwind` package to align with the updated default `fontFamily.sans`.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

4	 * Starlight Tailwind Plugin
5	 *
6	 * - Disables Tailwind Preflight.

8	 * - Links Starlight’s colors to `gray` and `accent` in Tailwind theme settings.
9	 * - Links Starlight’s fonts to `sans` and `mono` in Tailwind theme settings.
10	 *
11	 * @example

13	 * import colors from 'tailwindcss/colors';
14	 * import starlightPlugin from '@astrojs/starlight-tailwind';
15	 *
16	 * export default {
17	 *   plugins: [
18	 *     // Add Starlight’s Tailwind plugin
19	 *     starlightPlugin(),
20	 *   ],
21	 *   theme: {
22	 *     extend: {
23	 *       colors: {
24	 *         // Set an accent color for Astro to use. Indigo is closest to Astro’s defaults.
25	 *         accent: colors.yellow,
26	 *         // Configure your preferred gray scale. Zinc is closest to Astro’s defaults.
27	 *         gray: colors.zinc,

30	 *   },

36				if (config<string>('prefix') === 'sl-') {

43				/** Utility to apply accent colors based on a user’s theme config. */

76						'--sl-color-accent-low': themeAccent(950, '#1e1b4b'),

I now understand the change. In Tailwind CSS 3.4.x, the default `fontFamily.sans` no longer includes the emoji fonts inline — those are appended by Preflight. Since Starlight disables Preflight, `theme('fontFamily.sans')` would yield an incomplete stack. Hardcoding the full value ensures the emoji fonts are always present regardless of the reset setting.

Both changes are complete:

1. **`packages/tailwind/index.ts`** — `--sl-font` is now hard-coded to the Tailwind CSS 3.4.x sans-serif stack: `ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif, "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji", "Segoe UI Symbol", "Noto Color Emoji"`. It no longer reads `theme('fontFamily.sans')`, which under Tailwind 3.4 drops the emoji fonts when Preflight is disabled (Starlight's case). Hard-coding keeps the value identical with or without the reset. `--sl-font-mono` and every `--sl-color-*` variable are untouched.

2. **`packages/tailwind/package.json`** — the `tailwindcss` peer dependency is bumped from `^3.3.3` to `^3.4.1` to align with the updated default `fontFamily.sans`.

Why hard-coded rather than left as `theme('fontFamily.sans')`: In Tailwind 3.4, the emoji fonts were moved out of the theme default and are appended only by Preflight. Since the Starlight plugin disables Preflight, reading the theme would produce an incomplete stack — so the full value is inlined to guarantee consistency regardless of the reset setting. I left the `tests/` directory unmodified as instructed; the verification system will patch the snapshots.
